stem:
Navya rubs a plastic scale on a dry woollen sweater. Tiny aluminium foil bits jump onto the scale. She rubs a second identical plastic scale the same way and brings the two charged scales near each other.

Which claim correctly predicts what happens?

options.text: The two like-charged scales repel each other.
The two like-charged scales attract each other.
The scales attract foil bits only while they still touch the sweater.
The scales must be bar magnets because the foil bits moved.

teacher.key_rationale: Like charges repel, so two scales charged the same way push apart. Attracting like charges reverses the rule; needing ongoing contact with the sweater drops a true condition; calling the effect magnetism swaps the force type.
